title: Batch Image Generation API Options: 8 Providers on Batch and Webhooks

tools.name: Wireflow
tools.tagline: Best overall for running a multi-step batch from one request
tools.modelSupport: 100+ image, video and audio models as nodes

quickstart.label: Run a saved workflow from code: send its input values to this endpoint with an API key, then poll the execution or add a webhook block. The request format is in the API reference linked under Docs.

tools.moneyPageLabel: Wireflow node based image generation page

tools.name: OpenAI API
tools.tagline: Best for large batches that can wait a day
tools.modelSupport: Image generation and edits in the Batch API
tools.note: The linked repository is the official Python SDK. The Batch API is a hosted service.

quickstart.label: Create a batch from an uploaded file, from the OpenAI Batch guide. The guide's example targets /v1/chat/completions. For images, set the endpoint to /v1/images/generations or /v1/images/edits, which the guide lists as supported.

tools.name: Google Gemini API
tools.tagline: Best for image batches on Google models
tools.modelSupport: Gemini image generation in batch jobs
tools.note: The linked repository is the Google GenAI SDK for Python. The pricing page describes a free tier with limited access to certain models. Check that page for whether batch jobs are covered.

quickstart.label: Create a batch job with inline requests, from the Gemini Batch API guide. The guide's image example adds a responseModalities setting to each request and recommends a JSONL file for image generation.

tools.name: Runware
tools.tagline: Best for many image tasks in one request
tools.modelSupport: Image, video, audio, LLM and 3D models
tools.note: The linked repository is the official Python SDK. A TypeScript SDK is documented as well.

quickstart.label: Send one image task, from the Runware Models API introduction. The request body is an array, so more task objects can go in the same call.
quickstart.code:
curl https://api.runware.ai/v1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RUNWARE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '[
    {
      "taskType": "imageInference",
      "taskUUID": "a770f077-f413-47de-9dac-be0b26a35da6",
      "model": "xai:grok-imagine@image-quality",
      "positivePrompt": "A golden retriever on a park bench, cinematic lighting",
      "width": 1024,
      "height": 1024
    }
  ]'

tools.name: fal
tools.tagline: Best for a per-image queue across many hosted models
tools.note: The linked repository is the official JavaScript client. The Python client lives in fal-ai/fal.

quickstart.label: Submit a queued request with a webhook URL, from the fal webhooks docs.
quickstart.code:
curl --request POST \
  --url 'https://queue.fal.run/fal-ai/flux/dev?fal_webhook=https://url.to.your.app/api/fal/webhook' \
  --header "Authorization: Key $FAL_KEY" \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
  "prompt": "Photo of a cute dog"
}'

tools.name: Replicate
tools.tagline: Best for a per-image queue over open and official models
tools.modelSupport: Open and official models, plus your own
tools.note: The linked repository is the official Python client. JavaScript, Swift and Go clients are listed as well.

quickstart.label: Create a prediction with a completion webhook, from Replicate's create a prediction page.

tools.name: Black Forest Labs API
tools.tagline: Best for calling FLUX models directly
tools.note: No official SDK repository is named in the docs index, so none is listed in the data table.

quickstart.label: Submit a request and read the polling URL, from the Black Forest Labs integration guide. The guide then polls that URL until the status is Ready.
quickstart.code:
response=$(curl -X 'POST' \
  'https://api.bfl.ai/v1/flux-2-pro-preview' \
  -H 'accept: application/json' \
  -H "x-key: ${BFL_API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "prompt": "A serene landscape with mountains",
    "width": 1440,
    "height": 810
  }')

request_id=$(echo $response | jq -r .id)
polling_url=$(echo $response | jq -r .polling_url)

tools.name: Leonardo AI
tools.tagline: Best for outputs that should stay hosted
tools.modelSupport: Image generation, including your own custom models
tools.note: The linked repository is the official Python SDK.

quickstart.label: Create a generation, from Leonardo's quick start guide. The response returns a generation ID to poll.
quickstart.code:
curl --request POST \
     --url https://cloud.leonardo.ai/api/rest/v1/generations \
     --header 'accept: application/json' \
     --header 'authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>' \
     --header 'content-type: application/json' \
     --data '
{
  "alchemy": false,
  "height": 1080,
  "modelId": "7b592283-e8a7-4c5a-9ba6-d18c31f258b9",
  "contrast": 3.5,
  "num_images": 4,
  "styleUUID": "111dc692-d470-4eec-b791-3475abac4c46",
  "prompt": "A serene watercolor painting of a mountain lake at sunrise",
  "width": 1920,
  "ultra": false
}
'
